Silla
SIL-lah
n. (a place near Jerusalem, by the house of Millo, where Joash was slain)
Hebrew Silla, perhaps a highway or an embankment, from salal, to cast up a road; named once, at 2 Kings 12:20.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · In the Text · Related

Biblical Definition

Silla is named once, and only to fix the spot where a king of Judah was murdered by his own servants. The historian closes the reign in the usual form: “And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” (2 Kings 12:19), and then reports the end: “And his servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and slew Joash in the house of Millo, which goeth down to Silla” (2 Kings 12:20). The assassins are named: “For Jozachar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, smote him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Amaziah his son reigned in his stead” (2 Kings 12:21). The Chronicler supplies the reason, which Kings leaves out: “And when they were departed from him, (for they left him in great diseases,) his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings” (2 Chronicles 24:25). Joash had been saved as an infant by the priest Jehoiada, reigned well while that man lived, and then had Jehoiada's son stoned in the temple court.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Silla is a Hebrew proper name and has no entry in Webster's dictionary of the English language.

expand to see more

Silla is a Hebrew proper name; Webster's 1828 dictionary treats common English words and does not define it.

It is named once, at 2 Kings 12:20.

The name perhaps signifies a highway or an embankment.

It lay below the house of Millo, near Jerusalem.

Joash king of Judah was slain by his servants there.

Key Scripture

2Ki 12:19 — "And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?"

2Ki 12:20 — "And his servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and slew Joash in the house of Millo, which goeth down to Silla."

2Ki 12:21 — "For Jozachar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, smote him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Amaziah his son reigned in his stead."

2Ch 24:25 — "And when they were departed from him, (for they left him in great diseases,) his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings."

Modern Corruption

A good beginning is counted a finished work; Joash reigned well while Jehoiada lived and murdered Jehoiada's son afterward.

expand to see more

Joash was hidden in the temple as a baby, crowned at seven by the priest who saved him, and repaired the house of the LORD. When Jehoiada died he turned, and had Zechariah the son of Jehoiada stoned in the court of the house of God. His own servants killed him for that blood, and he was buried in the city but not in the sepulchres of the kings.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that a man borrowing another man's godliness has none of his own, and that God requires the blood of His servants at the hands of those who shed it.
